dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not suppress exceptions in `_register_contract_once`; let a registration failure raise (or assert `CONTRACT_NAME in _CONTRACTS` after registering) so the contract cannot silently fall back to the default findings model.

scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:366 calls `register_contract(CONTRACT_NAME, _build_contract)` at module scope WITHOUT suppression — the pattern this module claims to reuse does not swallow the error.
dropped.finding: `_register_contract_once` swallows all exceptions from `register_contract`, and an unregistered output_schema silently falls back to the default findings model (rebar.llm.contracts.response_model_for returns findings.findings_response_model() for an unknown/unregistered name). If registration fails, the run yields a generic findings dict instead of a RichTextRca, and nothing detects it.
scenarios: A pydantic import error or a typo in _build_contract raises during registration; the contract is never registered and the run produces a findings-shaped payload that passes the final assertion.
A future refactor makes register_contract raise on a duplicate/invalid name; the probe silently degrades to the default schema.
dropped.suggested_fix: Drop the `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` and call `register_contract(CONTRACT_NAME, _build_contract)` directly (idempotent re-registration is harmless), or follow with `assert response_model_for(CONTRACT_NAME) is not findings.findings_response_model()`.
